comments.text:
Fish can swim in and out of the Sargasso Sea, so to me, it's just an arbitrary categorization made by humans, not an actual distinct body of water. 
It's a model we use to identify a region within the Atlantic Ocean based on currents and ecological characteristics, but ultimately, it's all just the Atlantic Ocean. 
To the animals living there, it doesn't matter what we call it.

replies.author: @abveggieman
replies.text:
Aren’t all of our categorizations arbitrary? The Atlantic is connected to other oceans, it’s not completely cut off but we CHOOSE to distinguish it for ourselves. 

There is no such thing as a truly distinct body of water bc water is all connected to each other, you just have to zoom out far enough to see it. Even a lake with no streams flowing from it is a part of a water table and is a part of the water cycle. 

Maybe a better way of thinking about it is that the categorizations are not arbitrary, but they serve some purpose for conveying specific important information. In this case, it’s that the Sargasso Sea does not behave in the same way as the waters around it and is characterized by different weather, flora and fauna, etc.
